[`cppFUN()`](../reference/cppFUN.html) compiles a system of algebraic equations $y = g(x, p)$,
evaluated on the rows of a matrix of variables $x$ with parameters $p$ shared by all rows, with
first and second derivatives. Typical uses are observation functions and reparameterizations of the
inputs of `solveODE()`. The equations follow the
[expression language](../reference/expressions.html) of `cppODE()`; the generated code is
described in [Derivative directions of cppFUN()](methods-cppfun.html).

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Function definition

`variables` are given per row, `parameters` once; `variables` defaults to all symbols of the
equations not in `parameters` ([`getSymbols()`](../reference/getSymbols.html)). `derivMode` names
the derivative products built, any of `"forward"` (default: `jac`, `hess`, `evaluate`,
`evaluateBatch`), `"reverse"` (`vjp`) and `"forward-reverse"` (`vjp` with curvature); `deriv2 = TRUE`
adds the second derivatives, `deriv = FALSE` builds `func` alone, and `fixed` excludes symbols from
differentiation at compile time. As with `cppODE()`, `compile = FALSE` (here the default) writes
the source to `outdir` for a joint `compile()`.

The guide uses an observable $y = s(A + B)$ of the decay chain and the fraction
$z = B/(A + B)$, a reparameterization $k_i = \exp(\lambda_i)$, and an error model
$\sigma = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 B^2}$.

```{r models}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

chain  <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "g7_chain", compile = FALSE)
chainR <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", modelname = "g7_chainR", compile = FALSE)

obs   <- c(y = "s*(A + B)", z = "B/(A + B)")
g     <- cppFUN(obs, variables = c("A", "B"), parameters = "s", deriv2 = TRUE,
                derivMode = c("forward", "forward-reverse"), modelname = "g7_obs")
gM    <- cppFUN(obs, variables = c("A", "B"), parameters = "s", convenient = FALSE,
                modelname = "g7_obsM")
trafo <- cppFUN(c(k1 = "exp(lk1)", k2 = "exp(lk2)"), variables = character(0),
                parameters = c("lk1", "lk2"), modelname = "g7_trafo")
err   <- cppFUN(c(sigma = "sqrt(a^2 + b^2*B^2)"), variables = "B", parameters = c("a", "b"),
                modelname = "g7_err")

compile(chain, chainR, g, gM, trafo, err, output = "guide7", cores = 2)
```

## Values and derivatives

The returned list holds `func`, `jac`, `hess`, `evaluate`, `evaluateBatch` and `vjp`, each `NULL`
when not built. They take the inputs as named arguments, a variable as a vector with one element
per row. `func` returns the outputs, [row, output].

```{r func}
g$func(A = c(0.2, 0.1), B = c(0.5, 0.4), s = 2)
```

`jac` returns the first derivatives, [row, output, direction], by default in the variables and the
parameters; `fixed` excludes parameters at run time.

```{r jac}
g$jac(A = 0.2, B = 0.5, s = 2)[1, , ]
dimnames(g$jac(A = 0.2, B = 0.5, s = 2, fixed = "s"))[[3]]
```

`hess` returns the second derivatives, [row, output, direction, direction]; `evaluate` returns
value, first and, with `deriv2 = TRUE`, second derivatives from one pass.

```{r hess}
g$hess(A = 0.2, B = 0.5, s = 2)[1, "z", , ]
names(g$evaluate(A = 0.2, B = 0.5, s = 2, deriv2 = TRUE))
```

## Chain rule with ODE sensitivities

`tangentX`, [row, variable, direction], and `tangentP`, [parameter, direction], are the
derivatives of the inputs in the directions $\theta$; `hessianX` and `hessianP` are the second
derivatives. The results are then derivatives in $\theta$. With the sensitivities of the chain as
`tangentX` and a unit row for $s$ as `tangentP`, `evaluate` returns the observables with their
derivatives in $\theta = (A_0, B_0, k_1, k_2, s)$:

```{r observables}
out    <- solveODE(chain, times, parms)
theta  <- c(dimnames(out$tangent)[[3]], "s")
tangX  <- array(0, c(length(out$time), 2, length(theta)),
                dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"), theta))
tangX[, , 1:4] <- out$tangent
tangP  <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1), 1, dimnames = list("s", theta))

obsOut <- g$evaluate(A = out$variable[, "A"], B = out$variable[, "B"], s = 2,
                     tangentX = tangX, tangentP = tangP)
obsOut$tangent[101, , ]
```

```{r observables-plot, fig.height = 4.2}
traj <- list(time = out$time, variable = obsOut$y, tangent = obsOut$tangent)
ggplot(longFormat(traj, "y"), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

A tangent not given as an argument is taken from attribute `"deriv"` of the variables or
parameters, a second derivative from attribute `"deriv2"`.

## Reparameterization

A function of the parameters alone has no variables and one row. The Jacobian, rows named by the
outputs, is a partial `tangent` of `solveODE()`: the sensitivities are then derivatives in the
logarithms $\lambda_i$ of the rate constants.

```{r trafo}
k <- trafo$evaluate(lk1 = log(0.5), lk2 = log(0.2))
k$y
outL <- solveODE(chain, times, c(A = 1, B = 0, k$y[1, ]), tangent = k$tangent[1, , ])
outL$tangent[101, "B", ]
out$tangent[101, "B", c("k1", "k2")] * c(0.5, 0.2)
```

## Vector-Jacobian products

`vjp` contracts a cotangent of the outputs, [row, output] or [row, output, seed], with the
Jacobian in one reverse sweep. It returns `cotangentX`, [row, variable, seed], and `cotangentP`,
[parameter, seed], summed over the rows because the parameters are shared. `cotangentX` is the
cotangent of the states for a reverse-mode `solveODE()`, so the gradient of $\sum_t y(t)$ in
$\theta$ takes two backward sweeps:

```{r vjp}
x <- out$variable
v <- g$vjp(vars = x, params = c(s = 2), cotangent = cbind(y = rep(1, nrow(x)), z = 0))
c(solveODE(chainR, times, parms, cotangent = v$cotangentX[, , 1])$cotangent[, 1],
  v$cotangentP[, 1])
colSums(obsOut$tangent[, "y", ])
```

Under `"forward-reverse"`, `vjp` also takes `tangentX`, `tangentP` and `curvature`, the derivative
of the cotangent along the tangent, and returns `curvatureX` and `curvatureP`, the derivative of
the contraction along the tangent ([forward over reverse](methods-forward-reverse.html)). These
seeds are positional. Along $k_1$:

```{r vjp-curvature}
vk <- g$vjp(vars = x, params = c(s = 2), cotangent = cbind(y = rep(1, nrow(x)), z = 0),
            tangentX = tangX[, , "k1", drop = FALSE], tangentP = tangP[, "k1", drop = FALSE])
vk$curvatureP[, , 1]
sum(out$tangent[, c("A", "B"), "k1"])
```

## Matrix interface

With `convenient = FALSE`, `func`, `jac`, `hess` and `evaluate` take a matrix `vars`, columns
named by the variables, and a named vector `params`; `evaluateBatch` and `vjp` always do.
`attach.input = TRUE` appends the inputs that are neither variables nor parameters to the result.

```{r matrix}
gM$func(vars = cbind(x[1:3, ], time = out$time[1:3]), params = c(s = 2, dose = 1),
        attach.input = TRUE)
```

## Argument sets in one call

`evaluateBatch(sets, cores, deriv2)` runs `evaluate` over a list of argument sets, each with
`vars`, `params` and optionally the seeds, `fixed` and `attach.input`, in one call and on `cores`
threads. Here the observables at three scales:

```{r evaluateBatch}
sets <- lapply(c(1, 2, 4), function(s) list(vars = x[c(11, 51, 101), ], params = c(s = s)))
sapply(g$evaluateBatch(sets, cores = 2), function(r) r$y[, "y"])
```

[`evaluateMany()`](../reference/evaluateMany.html) evaluates one argument set for each of several
functions, here observable and error model, in one call and one parallel region.

```{r evaluateMany}
many <- evaluateMany(list(g$evaluateBatch, err$evaluateBatch),
                     list(list(vars = x[c(11, 51, 101), ], params = c(s = 2)),
                          list(vars = x[c(11, 51, 101), "B", drop = FALSE],
                               params = c(a = 0.01, b = 0.1))),
                     cores = 2)
many[[2]]$y
many[[2]]$tangent[, "sigma", ]
```
